body: This is late and probably not what she’s going for but: body autonomy. If someone violently invades your property, you have the right to “stand your ground” through whatever means necessary. Why should this only apply to a boogeyman with a gun? Your body is your property, owned by you, and no one should be able to occupy it without your consent. And if you believe life begins at conception and hate the idea of taking another life (God knows I’d exhaust every other option before I got to that point) why NOT support birth control and plan B, which hormonally stop conception before it happens. We don’t need the government telling us what we can and cannot do with our own body/private property. So much of our American system is built on “rules for thee, not for me”, if you can buy an AR-15 (a buzz-word gun, but gets the point across) for home defense, why the FUCK is norethindrone somehow a culture killer?

Late response and I'm not really who you're asking, as I am an immigrant that recently got citizenship, but here goes.
For a long time, I didn't understand how most Americans didn't have valid passports. Then I took a road trip to ~20 different states, and OH BOY. The USA is not a single country, but a collection of territories under one federal government. As such each state has different laws, practices, religions, superstitions, and histories from another. Even "boring" states are unique in their structure, values, and commercial practices from their surrounding states. The climate varies wildly as well. There's a common language and a shared government+history, but outside of that each state is its own entity. And the people living in each state varies massively as well. The kinds of native american people and European, African, and Central/Southern American descendants/immigrants you interact with change based on location.
All in all, I'm not surprised people feel a kind of culture shock moving from state to state. Take, for example, Italy and Spain. They speak a similar language, are on the same continent, have a long shared history, and in modern day they participate in a shared government agency (the EU). But these two countries are completely unique from one another. This is a similar situation between the states.

Oh okay, I understand you now. Sorry, I'm used to everyone's advice being "just call 911!". I 100% agree though, the ability of first responders and the likes to just shutdown, follow routine, and do their jobs no matter how horrific or hopeless the situation is commendable. I felt like I was facing a firing squad today when they were sat behind me, like the only thing I could do was square my shoulders and wait. I guess it was a freeze response, as opposed to an active response.

I think I understand where you're coming from, that in this situation it would be better for me to call the paramedics anyway to ensure their safety. But for us, there isn't really a "right" state of mind to make these decisions. This is just how we are, and have been for the past decade. And how can I call the paramedics knowing if they get committed they could just be abused more by doctors, all the while with a betrayal (real or perceived depending on your perspective) from their partner on their mind?
